West Berkshire's population increased by around 7,600 between the last two censuses (held in 2011 and 2021). This semi-automated article highlights some of the most notable changes among the local population.

The population passed 160,000

Between the last two censuses (held in 2011 and 2021), the population of West Berkshire increased by 5.0%, from around 153,800 in 2011 to around 161,400 in 2021.

The population here increased by a smaller percentage than the overall population of the South East (7.5%), and by a smaller percentage than the overall population of England (up 6.6% since the 2011 Census).

In 2021, West Berkshire was home to around 1.6 people per football pitch-sized piece of land. This area was among the lowest 25% for population density across English local authority areas at the last census.

This article generally uses percentages to enable comparisons over time and between areas. The percentage point change is also used to show the difference between the 2011 and 2021 percentages.

Population growth was lower in West Berkshire than across the South East

An older West Berkshire

Between the last two censuses, the average (median) age of West Berkshire increased by three years, from 40 to 43 years of age.

This area had a higher average (median) age than the South East as a whole in 2021 (41 years) and a higher average (median) age than England (40 years).

The median age is the age of the person in the middle of the group, meaning that one half of the group is younger than that person and the other half is older.

The number of people aged 65 to 74 years rose by around 4,100 (an increase of 31.7%), while the number of residents between 35 and 49 years fell by around 4,000 (11.2% decrease).

The share of residents aged between 65 and 74 years increased by 2.1 percentage points between 2011 and 2021

Change in employment

West Berkshire saw the South East's second-largest percentage-point fall in the proportion of people aged 16 years and over (excluding full-time students) who were employed (from 65.0% in 2011 to 61.7% in 2021).

Across the region, only West Oxfordshire saw a greater fall in the percentage of people aged 16 years and over (excluding full-time students) who were employed (from 65.1% to 61.7%).

Despite the decrease, West Berkshire was in the highest 10% of English local authority areas for the share of people aged 16 years and over (excluding full-time students) who were employed in 2021.

Census 2021 took place during the coronavirus (COVID-19) pandemic, a period of rapid and unparalleled change; the national lockdown, associated guidance and furlough measures will have affected the labour market and our ability to measure it.

The percentage of people aged 16 years and over who were employed (excluding full-time students) in West Berkshire decreased by 3.3 percentage points

Fewer adults working long hours

West Berkshire saw the South East's joint third-largest percentage-point fall (alongside Wokingham) in the proportion of people aged 16 years and over and in employment who said they usually worked over 49 hours per week (from 16.1% in 2011 to 12.4% in 2021).

Across the region, only Bracknell Forest (from 15.8% to 11.7%) and Surrey Heath (from 16.9% to 12.9%) saw a greater decrease in the percentage of people aged 16 years and over and in employment who said they usually worked over 49 hours per week.

Every local authority area across the South East saw a fall in the percentage of people aged 16 years and over and in employment who said they usually worked over 49 hours per week, as the regional percentage fell from 14.6% to 11.9%.

Working hours may have been affected by the coronavirus (COVID-19) pandemic.

The percentage of adults in employment who worked 49 hours or more in West Berkshire decreased by 3.7 percentage points

Rise in private renting

Of West Berkshire households, 17.1% rented privately in 2021, up from 13.7% in 2011.

In 2021, just under one in seven households (14.0%) lived in socially rented housing, compared with 13.8% in 2011. The percentage of West Berkshire households that owned their home (outright or with a mortgage or loan) decreased from 69.7% to 67.6%.

The increase in the percentage of privately-rented homes was greater in West Berkshire (3.4 percentage points) than across the South East (2.9 percentage points, from 16.3% to 19.2%). Across England, the percentage increased by 3.6 percentage points, from 16.8% to 20.5%.

Private renting in West Berkshire increased by 3.4 percentage points

Unpaid care in West Berkshire

In 2021, 4.4% of West Berkshire residents (aged five years and over) reported providing up to 19 hours of unpaid care each week. This figure decreased from 7.2% in 2011. These are age-standardised proportions.

Age-standardised proportions are used throughout this section. They enable comparisons between populations over time and across geographies, as they account for differences in the population size and age structure.

In 2021, 1.3% of residents (aged five years and over) reported providing between 20 and 49 hours of unpaid care each week, compared with 1.0% in 2011. The proportion of West Berkshire residents (aged five years and over) that provided at least 50 hours of weekly unpaid care increased from 1.8% to 2.1%.

The decrease in the proportion of people (aged five years and over) providing up to 19 hours of weekly unpaid care in West Berkshire (2.8 percentage points) was similar to the decrease across the South East (2.8 percentage points, from 7.3% to 4.5%). Across England, the proportion fell by 2.8 percentage points, from 7.2% to 4.4%.

Census 2021 was undertaken during the coronavirus (COVID-19) pandemic. This may have influenced how people perceived and managed their provision of unpaid care, and therefore may have affected how people chose to respond.

Caution should be taken when making comparisons between 2011 and 2021 because of changes in question wording and response options.

The percentage of people (aged five years and over) providing up to 19 hours of weekly unpaid care in West Berkshire decreased by 2.8 percentage points

Religion in West Berkshire

In 2021, 41.1% of West Berkshire residents reported having "No religion", up from 26.7% in 2011. The rise of 14.4 percentage points was the largest increase of all broad religious groups in West Berkshire. Because the census question about religious affiliation is voluntary and has varying response rates, caution is needed when comparing figures between different areas or between censuses.

Across the South East, the percentage of residents who described themselves as having "No religion" increased from 27.7% to 40.2%, while across England the percentage increased from 24.8% to 36.7%.

In 2021, 49.1% of people in West Berkshire described themselves as Christian (down from 63.6%), while 6.1% did not state their religion (down from 7.2% the decade before).

There are many factors that can cause changes to the religious profile of an area, such as a changing age structure or residents relocating for work or education. Changes may also be caused by differences in the way individuals chose to self-identify between censuses. Religious affiliation is the religion with which someone connects or identifies, rather than their beliefs or religious practice.

West Berkshire residents' country of birth

In the latest census, around 136,600 West Berkshire residents said they were born in England. This represented 84.6% of the local population. The figure has risen from just over 133,900 in 2011, which at the time represented 87.1% of West Berkshire's population.

Scotland was the next most represented, with just under 2,500 West Berkshire residents reporting this country of birth (1.5%). This figure was down from around 2,900 in 2011, which at the time represented 1.9% of the population of West Berkshire.

The number of West Berkshire residents born in Wales fell from around 2,500 in 2011 (1.6% of the local population) to around 2,300 in 2021 (1.4%).

In 2021, 84.6% of West Berkshire residents reported their country of birth as England

National identity in West Berkshire

In 2021, 6.5% of West Berkshire residents did not identify with any national identity associated with the UK. This figure increased from 4.9% in 2011.

In 2021, just over 1 in 50 people (2.1%) identified with a UK and non-UK national identity, compared with 0.9% in 2011. The percentage of residents in West Berkshire that identified as "British only" increased from 17.1% to 56.4%.

The increase in the percentage of people who did not identify with any national identity associated with the UK in West Berkshire (1.6 percentage points) was similar to the increase across the South East (1.6 percentage points, from 7.1% to 8.7%). Across England, the percentage increased by 1.7 percentage points, from 8.2% to 10.0%.

In Census 2021, “British” was moved to the top response option and this may have influenced how people described their national identity. For further information, please see our quality report.

The percentage of people who did not identify with at least one UK national identity in West Berkshire increased by 1.6 percentage points

Fewer couples without children

Of West Berkshire households, 19.1% included a couple but no children in 2021, down from 21.5% in 2011.

The decrease in the percentage of households including a couple but no children was greater in West Berkshire (2.4 percentage points) than across the South East (1.4 percentage points, from 18.7% to 17.4%). Across England, the percentage fell by 0.9 percentage points, from 17.6% to 16.8%.

The percentage of households including a couple without children in West Berkshire decreased by 2.4 percentage points

More adults never married or in a civil partnership

Of West Berkshire residents aged 16 years and over, 31.5% said they had never been married or in a civil partnership in 2021, up from 28.6% in 2011.

In 2021, just over one in two people (51.6%) said they were married or in a registered civil partnership, compared with 54.2% in 2011. The percentage of adults in West Berkshire that had divorced or dissolved a civil partnership increased from 8.8% to 9.1%.

The increase in the percentage of people aged 16 years and over who had never been married or in a civil partnership in West Berkshire (2.9 percentage points) was similar to the increase across the South East (2.9 percentage points, from 31.9% to 34.8%). Across England, the percentage increased by 3.3 percentage points, from 34.6% to 37.9%.

These figures include same-sex marriages and opposite-sex civil partnerships in 2021, neither of which were legally recognised in England and Wales in 2011. Same-sex marriages have been legally recognised in England and Wales since 2014 and opposite-sex civil partnerships have been recognised since 2019.

The percentage of adults who had never married or registered a civil partnership in West Berkshire increased by 2.9 percentage points

Disability in West Berkshire

In 2021, 5.1% of West Berkshire residents were identified as being disabled and limited a lot. This figure decreased from 6.1% in 2011. These are age-standardised proportions.

Age-standardised proportions are used throughout this section. They enable comparisons between populations over time and across geographies, as they account for differences in the population size and age structure.

In 2021, just under 1 in 10 people (9.6%) were identified as being disabled and limited a little, compared with 8.7% in 2011. The proportion of West Berkshire residents who were not disabled increased from 85.2% to 85.3%.

The decrease in the proportion of residents who were identified as being disabled and limited a lot in West Berkshire (1.0 percentage points) was similar to the decrease across the South East (1.0 percentage points, from 7.2% to 6.2%). Across England, the proportion fell by 1.6 percentage points, from 9.1% to 7.5%.

Census 2021 was undertaken during the coronavirus (COVID-19) pandemic. This may have influenced how people perceived their health status and activity limitations, and therefore may have affected how people chose to respond.

Caution should be taken when making comparisons between 2011 and 2021 because of changes in question wording and response options.

The percentage of people who were identified as being disabled and limited a lot in West Berkshire decreased by 1.0 percentage points

Health in West Berkshire

In 2021, 50.9% of West Berkshire residents described their health as "very good", increasing from 49.4% in 2011. Those describing their health as "good" fell from 35.3% to 34.8%. These are age-standardised proportions.

Age-standardised proportions are used throughout this section. They enable comparisons between populations over time and across geographies, as they account for differences in the population size and age structure.

The proportion of West Berkshire residents describing their health as "very bad" was 0.7% (similar to 2011), while those describing their health as "bad" was 2.7% (similar to 2011).

These data reflect people’s own opinions in describing their overall health on a five point scale, from very good to very bad.

Census 2021 was conducted during the coronavirus (COVID-19) pandemic. This may have influenced how people perceived and rated their health, and therefore may have affected how people chose to respond.

The percentage of people in very good health in West Berkshire increased by 1.5 percentage points

Ethnic groups in West Berkshire

In 2021, 3.7% of West Berkshire residents identified their ethnic group within the "Asian, Asian British or Asian Welsh" category, up from 2.5% in 2011. The 1.2 percentage-point change was the largest increase among high-level ethnic groups in this area.

Across the South East, the percentage of people from the "Asian, Asian British or Asian Welsh" ethnic group increased from 5.2% to 7.0%, while across England the percentage increased from 7.8% to 9.6%.

In 2021, 91.9% of people in West Berkshire identified their ethnic group within the "White" category (compared with 94.8% in 2011), while 2.4% identified their ethnic group within the "Mixed or Multiple" category (compared with 1.6% the previous decade).

The percentage of people who identified their ethnic group within the "Black, Black British, Black Welsh, Caribbean or African" category increased from 0.9% in 2011 to 1.3% in 2021.

There are many factors that may be contributing to the changing ethnic composition of England and Wales, such as differing patterns of ageing, fertility, mortality, and migration. Changes may also be caused by differences in the way individuals chose to self-identify between censuses.
